content.title: About
content.content: Spinach‑filled tortellini are small ring‑shaped pasta parcels stuffed with fresh spinach, often combined with ricotta or parmesan. They are served in a fragrant tomato sauce that highlights the delicate filling and makes the dish hearty and flavorful.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tortellini originate from Italy, especially the Emilia‑Romagna and Tuscany regions.
Traditionally they are hand‑shaped, but modern production often uses specialized molding machines.
Spinach gives the filling a vivid green color and boosts its nutritional profile.
Tomato sauce is typically made from ripe tomatoes, olive oil, garlic, and basil.
Tortellini are a popular choice for festive meals, particularly during Christmas and New Year celebrations.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Spinach provides a good amount of iron, essential for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes are high in lycopene, while spinach supplies lutein; both help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from spinach and whole‑grain flour in the dough promotes healthy bowel function.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Tortellini deliver plant protein from spinach and dairy, as well as wheat protein from the pasta.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: The dish contains no added sugars, making it suitable for moderate consumption.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: The dough is traditionally made from wheat flour, so the product is not suitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Lactose
items.content: If ricotta or parmesan is used in the filling, the dish may contain lactose.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Tomato sauce often contains salt; those monitoring sodium intake should watch portion size.

items.title: Spinach allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may be allergic to spinach or other leafy greens.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the tortellini hot, drenched in tomato sauce. Sprinkle with grated parmesan, add fresh basil or a drizzle of olive oil. They pair well with a light salad or vegetable side dish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Dry tortellini should be kept in an airtight container in a cool, dry place for up to 12 months. Cooked tortellini can be stored in the refrigerator in a sealed container for 3‑4 days. For freezing, place in a freezer‑safe bag and use within 2‑3 months.
